passage:
Looking back, I expected the worst. My laptop bag had been stolen from a café near the bus stand, and I walked into the police station rehearsing an apology for wasting their time.

The officer at the desk, Sub-Inspector Anirban, offered me water and asked me to sit. He listened to the whole story without interrupting. I told him I had left the bag on the chair while I went to the counter. I almost skipped that part, but I told it straight. "That helps me," he said. "Now, what exactly was in the bag?"

He wrote the list with me, handed me a copy of the report, and added his number. A week later I called and he told me where the case stood. Nothing was recovered, but I had been treated like a person. I wrote him a thank-you note, and he pinned it on the board.

Dolma

qa.q: What did Dolma admit to the officer about the bag?
qa.a: Dolma admitted leaving the bag on the chair while going to the counter.

qa.q: What was Dolma expecting when walking into the police station?
qa.a: Dolma expected the worst and was rehearsing an apology for wasting their time, which shows a fear of being dismissed.

qa.q: What should someone do after reporting a theft?
qa.a: Cooperate honestly, keep the copy of the report, follow up by phone, and thank helpful officers, as Dolma did.

qa.q: How might Sub-Inspector Anirban have seen Dolma's honesty about the chair?
qa.a: As useful information: Anirban said "That helps me" and could then ask the right next questions.

grounding: A decent officer helps Dolma report a theft respectfully; Dolma cooperates honestly, follows up and thanks the officer.
